text.p: RAO Gazprom's 1995 profit before tax was 19.64 trillion roubles on sales of 71.44 trillion according to restated figures to Russian accounting standards audited by Price Waterhouse.
The new accounts made available to Reuters on Thursday by Gazprom did not contain comparative figures.
In May Gazprom said its 1995 profit before tax was 17.13 trillion roubles on sales of 123.28 trillion.
Profit and loss figures stated to international accounting standards were not available.
However Gazprom issued a balance sheet audited by Price Waterhouse to international accounting standards, which showed total assets at 367.74 trillion roubles at the end of 1995.
The balance sheet to Russian standards audited by Price Waterhouse showed assets at 244.51 trillion roubles.

Russian accounting standards differ significantly from those normally supplied in the West. Russian accounts are designed to meet the requirements of the tax authorities. Russian companies can choose whether to show revenues and spending on a cash or accruals basis. Definitions of profit and assets differ significantly from those in the West, and converting Russian accounts to international standards can turn a profit into a loss.
RAO Gazprom produces more than 90 percent of Russia's natural gas. It is Russia's biggest company by market capitalisation but its shares are highly illiquid.
It closed $0.005 up on the Russian Trading System on Thursday at $0.325.
Gazprom is preparing an international share issue later this year.
